# ScaleToFit

Header: `winui/ui/containers/ScaleToFit.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/containers/ScaleToFit.hpp`.

One child, laid out at its natural size and drawn scaled to the room the [ScaleToFit](#uiscaletofit) is given.

The child is measured with unbounded room, then drawn with a scale that [stretch()](#stretch) and [stretch_direction()](#stretch_direction) decide. The [ScaleToFit](#uiscaletofit) asks for the scaled size. [Text](../controls/text.md#uitext) is scaled like a picture and keeps its line breaks and font size. Pointer input is mapped back through the same scale, so the child's controls keep working at any size. A popup opened from inside is anchored where its owner would be unscaled. With UniformToFill, the overflow is clipped.

Example: 
```cpp
auto  box   = std::make_unique<ui::ScaleToFitControl>();
auto* label = box->set_child(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("42"));
box->set_stretch(ui::Stretch::Uniform);
box->set_stretch_direction(ui::StretchDirection::UpOnly); // grow the text, never shrink it
window.set_content(std::move(box));
label->set_text("43"); // the observer stays valid, and the next layout scales the new text

// Or declaratively, filling a 200x100 slot:
window.set_content(ui::ScaleToFit{
    .width   = 200.0f,
    .height  = 100.0f,
    .content = ui::Text{.text = "42"},
});
```

## `ui::ScaleToFit`

One child scaled to the room it is given. Builds a [ui::ScaleToFitControl](#uiscaletofitcontrol).

The child is measured at its natural size and then scaled, text and strokes included.

Example: 
```cpp
window.set_content(ui::ScaleToFit{
    .stretch           = ui::Stretch::Uniform,
    .stretch_direction = ui::StretchDirection::DownOnly, // shrink to fit, never enlarge
    .width             = 200.0f,
    .height            = 100.0f,
    .content           = ui::Text{.text = "Scaled to fit", .role = ui::TextRole::Header},
});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::ScaleToFit{
    .stretch, .stretch_direction, .style, .margin, .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height,
    .max_width, .max_height, .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip,
    .accessibility, .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus,
    .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control, .content
}
```

Fields, in declaration order (designators must follow it):

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="uiscaletofit-stretch"></span>`stretch` | `ui::Binding<ui::Stretch>` | `{ui::Stretch::Uniform}` | How the child's natural size maps to the box. Uniform, the default, keeps its aspect ratio. |
| <span id="uiscaletofit-stretch_direction"></span>`stretch_direction` | `ui::Binding<ui::StretchDirection>` | `{ui::StretchDirection::Both}` | UpOnly only enlarges, DownOnly only shrinks, and Both, the default, does both. |
| <span id="uiscaletofit-on_pointer_entered"></span>`on_pointer_entered` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer moved onto the control. |
| <span id="uiscaletofit-on_pointer_exited"></span>`on_pointer_exited` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer left the control. |
| <span id="uiscaletofit-on_got_focus"></span>`on_got_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus arrived on the control, or on anything inside it, from outside it. A control with nothing focusable in it never gets focus, and never raises this. |
| <span id="uiscaletofit-on_lost_focus"></span>`on_lost_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus left the control and everything inside it. |
| <span id="uiscaletofit-on_key_down"></span>`on_key_down` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::KeyEvent&)>` |  | A key pressed while focus is on the control or inside it, before the control's own handling; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_key_down()](../tree/element.md#on_key_down)). |
| <span id="uiscaletofit-on_wheel"></span>`on_wheel` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::PointerEvent&)>` |  | A wheel turn over the control, before the control scrolls; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_wheel()](../tree/element.md#on_wheel)). |
| <span id="uiscaletofit-control"></span>`control` | `ui::ControlOut<ui::ScaleToFit>` |  | Out: the handle that receives the built control. |
| <span id="uiscaletofit-content"></span>`content` | `ui::Spec` |  | The scaled child. |

Plus the common fields `style`, `margin`, `width`, `height`, `min_width`, `min_height`, `max_width`, `max_height`, `horizontal_alignment`, `vertical_alignment`, `visible`, `tool_tip`, `accessibility` every spec carries ([conventions](../conventions.md#common-fields-on-every-spec)).

### build

```cpp
std::unique_ptr<Element> build()&&
```

Consumes the spec and returns the built [ui::ScaleToFitControl](#uiscaletofitcontrol); the caller owns it.

## `ui::ScaleToFitControl`

Derives from `ui::Element`.

One child, laid out at its natural size and drawn scaled to the room the [ScaleToFit](#uiscaletofit) is given.

The child is measured with unbounded room, then drawn with a scale that [stretch()](#stretch) and [stretch_direction()](#stretch_direction) decide. The [ScaleToFit](#uiscaletofit) asks for the scaled size. [Text](../controls/text.md#uitext) is scaled like a picture and keeps its line breaks and font size. Pointer input is mapped back through the same scale, so the child's controls keep working at any size. A popup opened from inside is anchored where its owner would be unscaled. With UniformToFill, the overflow is clipped.

Example: 
```cpp
auto  box   = std::make_unique<ui::ScaleToFitControl>();
auto* label = box->set_child(std::make_unique<ui::TextControl>("42"));
box->set_stretch(ui::Stretch::Uniform);
box->set_stretch_direction(ui::StretchDirection::UpOnly); // grow the text, never shrink it
window.set_content(std::move(box));
label->set_text("43"); // the observer stays valid, and the next layout scales the new text

// Or declaratively, filling a 200x100 slot:
```

### ScaleToFitControl

```cpp
ScaleToFitControl() = default
```

An empty [ScaleToFit](#uiscaletofit), Uniform and Both.

### set_child

```cpp
template <typename T>
T* set_child(std::unique_ptr<T> child)
```

Takes ownership of the single child and returns a non-owning observer. Replaces and destroys any previous child, and nullptr clears it. Updates layout.

### child

```cpp
Element* child() const
```

The child, or nullptr. Owned by the [ScaleToFit](#uiscaletofit).

### stretch

```cpp
Stretch stretch() const
```

How the child is scaled. `Uniform` by default. None never scales, and [Fill](fill.md#uifill) scales each axis to its room. Uniform fits inside the room and UniformToFill covers it, both keeping the aspect ratio.

### set_stretch

```cpp
void set_stretch(Stretch stretch)
```

Changes the stretch. Updates layout.

### stretch_direction

```cpp
StretchDirection stretch_direction() const
```

Whether scaling may enlarge, shrink or both. `Both` by default.

### set_stretch_direction

```cpp
void set_stretch_direction(StretchDirection direction)
```

Changes which way scaling may go. Updates layout.

### scale_x

```cpp
float scale_x() const
```

The horizontal scale the child is drawn at, from the last arrange. 1 before the first.

### scale_y

```cpp
float scale_y() const
```

The vertical scale, like [scale_x()](#scale_x). The two differ only under Stretch::Fill.

### compute_scale_factor

```cpp
Size compute_scale_factor(Size available, Size content) const
```

The x and y factors that fit [`content`](../tree/spec-vocabulary.md#content) into `available` under the current [stretch()](#stretch) and [stretch_direction()](#stretch_direction). An unbounded axis ([ui::Unbounded](../core/namespace-ui.md#unbounded)) uses the other axis's factor. With both unbounded, the factors are 1 and 1.

### for_each_child

```cpp
void for_each_child(ChildVisitor visit) const override
```

The child, when there is one.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

Implement these instead of [measure()](../tree/element.md#measure) and [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange). The base class has already applied margin, size limits and alignment by the time these run. [measure_override()](#measure_override) is pure (every concrete [Element](../tree/element.md) must size itself); [arrange_override()](#arrange_override) defaults to a no-op since most leaves need nothing beyond having [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds) set, which the base already did.

### arrange_override

```cpp
void arrange_override(const Rect& final_rect, const ArrangeContext& context) override
```

Position children within the rect [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange) settled on (also in [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds), window DIPs). Default: nothing, for a leaf.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

What the control draws, in layout coordinates; [render()](../tree/element.md#render) has already applied the visual layer. A container draws its children through their [render()](../tree/element.md#render), never their [render_override()](#render_override).

### map_to_children

```cpp
Point map_to_children(Point p) const override
```

The point as the scaled child sees it.

### children_hit_clip

```cpp
std::optional<Rect> children_hit_clip() const override
```

The child is clipped to the bounds, and can be hit only inside them.

## Enumerations

### StretchDirection

```cpp
enum class StretchDirection
```

Which way a [ScaleToFit](#uiscaletofit) may scale its child.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `UpOnly` | Only enlarge. A child bigger than the room is drawn at its natural size. |
| `DownOnly` | Only shrink. A child smaller than the room is drawn at its natural size. |
| `Both` | The default. Scale either way. |
